item.title: The deterministic half of neuro-symbolic AI already exists. It's called network verification.
item.description:
Everybody’s suddenly got a take on neuro-symbolic AI. Inference for pattern recognition, symbolic logic paired in for reasoning you can actually trust, and the EU AI Act’s enforcement phase lighting a fire under all of it because “the model said so” stopped being an acceptable audit trail.

The pitch is real. Inference is powerful and unreliable, a statistical guess dressed up as an answer. Deterministic, mathematical models are reliable and narrow. Combining them, having the deterministic side check inference’s work, is turning into the actual path to AI you can trust in production. What’s less talked about: in networking, the deterministic half of that equation isn’t something you’d have to build. It already exists, and it’s been hardening in production for 7 years.

item.title: Delivering APIs for AI
item.description:
The rise of AI agents and autonomous systems is fundamentally changing how we design and deliver APIs, shifting from human-centric interfaces to AI-native integration patterns that require new architectural thinking.

The Inflection Point

Technology innovation has repeatedly transformed how we build systems. From the fourth-generation programming languages (4GL) of the 1990s that abstracted database operations to today’s AI-powered code generation, each wave has forced us to rethink fundamental assumptions. We now stand at another such inflection point: the transition from human-interface (HI) APIs to agent-interface (AI) APIs.
